newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila opens airstrip on disputed Spratly island.
newsitem.headline: Manila opens airstrip on disputed Spratly island.

text.p: The Philippines' armed forces chief formally opened on Christmas Day a runway on one of the disputed Spratly Islands and pledged to develop the area as a tourist spot, government television said.

General Arnulfo Acedera, accompanied by Manila newspaper reporters, also brought Christmas gifts to soldiers stationed on the Kalayaan (Freedom) island group, west of the main southwestern Philippine island of Palawan.
Manila claims ownership of the eight-island Kalayaan group in the Spratlys, a cluster of potentially oil-rich but largely uninhabited isles, shoals and reefs in the South China Sea.
The Spratlys are claimed wholly or in part by China, Taiwan, Vietnam, the Philippines, Malaysia and Brunei.

Acedera said in an interview on government television the purpose of his trip was to spread Christmas cheer to the troops, develop Kalayaan into a tourist destination and "officially open this runway to our C-130 operations." The C-130 is a military transport plane.

Tension between the Philippines and China flared in the area last year when Manila accused the Chinese of building what it said were possible naval structures on Mischief Reef, which Manila says is part of Kalayaan.
Beijing has refused to dismantle the structures, saying they are shelters for fishermen.

Chinese President Jiang Zemin and Philippine President Fidel Ramos agreed during Jiang's visit to Manila last month to shelve their two countries' differences over the Spratlys and consider cooperation in developing the area.
